subject: Pilot scope decision log: SDK changes, streaming & function-call clarifications
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@medbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-20T22:02:00Z
Subject: Pilot scope decision log: SDK changes, streaming & function-call clarifications

Michael — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick written summary so we have a single decision log to iterate on.

High-level pain / goals you confirmed on the call:
- Long medical records (multi-doc patient timelines) cause truncation and loss of context for summarization and triage.
- Existing embedding-based similarity search has noisy recall for note-level queries; you want reranking + dense retrieval hybrid.
- Need structured outputs (FHIR-ish summary, triage code) from model with deterministic field mapping for downstream systems.
- SLA constraints: 95th latency for interactive triage under 400ms for single-turn queries (target), batch rerank OK at higher tail.

Agreements & technical direction we discussed:
1) Streaming + function-calls: Redwood will provide an SDK streaming path that emits partial JSON-safe outputs and a final function-call payload to guarantee structured outputs. This avoids large single-token returns and enables progressive render in your UI.
2) Embeddings + rerank: pilot will use Medbridge embeddings (128-d) for index pruning, then an LLM reranker (Redwood hosted) for top-K re-score. We'll measure P@5 and latency impact.
3) SDK changes: we will ship a small client patch (JS + Python) that adds a streaming callback hook, a function-call schema validator, and a configurable KV cache TTL. Expect a PR-based draft within 5 business days.
4) Security / audit: we noted need for log redaction and retention controls; we will share SOC2 evidence and a proposed retention policy (attach).

Immediate next steps (owners & due dates):
- Redwood (Sofia): share pilot_scope_v1.xlsx and api_contract_draft.md (attached) — today.
- Medbridge (Michael): confirm primary dataset for rerank (10k notes sample) and share access method — by EOD 11/23.
- Redwood (Ben): draft SDK PR and performance baseline checklist — 11/25.
- Schedule: tech deep-dive (internal + engineers) week of 11/30 — propose 60m.

Attachments: pilot_scope_v1.xlsx (pilot matrix), api_contract_draft.md (API payload schema)

Thanks — I captured the decision items above so we can move directly to a technical kickoff.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@medbridge.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@novatrax.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot scope decision log: SDK changes, streaming & function-call clarifications

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority: Our immediate priority is the triage UI where clinicians need quick, structured summaries. If we have to postpone rerank improvements, structured/fn-call streaming is higher priority.
- Latency specifics: the 400ms target is for single document summarization at 95th pctl for a 2–4 KB input. For multi-document context (patient timeline) we can accept up to 1.5s with streaming enabled.
- Data access: we'll provision a sanitized 10k-notes S3 bucket (s3://medbridge-pilot/samples-10k) and provide temporary credentials to your team.

Also attaching a filled SOC2 questionnaire; there are a couple of control clarifications we will need during the pilot (access logs, key rotation cadence).

Can Ben weigh in quickly on the expected overhead for function-call wrapping + streaming on your hosted runtimes? If that looks heavy we may split the work: Redwood ships function-call & SDK patch first, rerank in a second sprint.

—
Michael Chen
Director of Product — Clinical AI, Medbridge Health
michael.chen@medbridge.ai

[Attachment: medbridge_soc2_questionnaire_filled.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Michael Chen <michael.chen@medbridge.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-23T11:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot scope decision log: SDK changes, streaming & function-call clarifications

Michael — quick tech note on expected overhead and implementation approach: 

1) Function-call + streaming overhead: the SDK streaming hook itself is lightweight — it emits serialized chunks as the model generates. The main overhead is maintaining the KV cache and orchestrating incremental schema validation. Based on similar pilots, expect a ~8–12% CPU/GPU utilization increase for interactive configs; token cost is unchanged aside from slight framing metadata.

2) Implementation plan (short):
- Day 0–2: SDK PR with streaming callback & json-schema validator (JS/Py).
- Day 3–7: Redwood CI build + internal perf baseline for a 2–4 KB document. We'll test against your 10k sample to measure 95th pctl.
- Sprint 2: rerank pipeline integration (index pruning -> top-50 rerank) and a small quantized model for cheaper rerank passes.

3) Parity notes: function-call schemas will be versioned; if you need strict FHIR mapping we can add a lightweight transformation layer in the SDK to map keys from model output to FHIR fields.

Action items from Ben:
- I will spin up a perf test harness and share baseline numbers by 11/25.
- Request: Michael — a sample 100-note set with labels for 5 queries would help tune the reranker quickly.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Thanks everyone — short status and proposed calendar: 

Status:
- Attachments: pilot_scope_v1.xlsx and api_contract_draft.md are attached in the original note. Ben will open the SDK PR on 11/25.
- Michael: we'll expect the sanitized 10k S3 bucket credentials by EOD 11/23 (if delayed, let us know).

Proposed calendar / next meetings:
- 11/25 10:00–11:00 PT: internal kickoff (Redwood eng + solutions) — Ben to host and share perf harness.
- 12/01 13:00–14:00 PT: technical deep dive (Medbridge engineering + Redwood) — invite to follow.

Deliverables & acceptance criteria for pilot MVP:
- Structured summaries via function-call payload with schema validation >= 90% field compliance on the 100-note test set.
- Interactive triage 95th pctl latency <= 400ms for single-doc summarization.
- Rerank P@5 improvement >= 12% over current baseline (measured on 10k sample).

If there are no objections I will lock the decision log and convert pilot_scope_v1.xlsx into a shared Drive folder with milestone trackers.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.
